ledger.x: 1922, 30 December: the Russian, Ukrainian, Byelorussian and Transcaucasian republics sign the treaty creating the Soviet Union.
1922: the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic stands inside the Union as a dependency.
1922: the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic stands inside the Union as a dependency (see the Bukharan republic).
1922: Tuva is a Soviet satellite, not Soviet land.
1924, 27 October: the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic ends and its land goes to the Uzbek, Turkmen and Tajik units of the Union.
1924, 27 October: the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic ends.

1924, 27 October: the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic is divided between the Uzbek SSR (West Bukhara), the Turkmen SSR (the south bank of the Amu Darya with Chardjui) and the Tajik ASSR (East Bukhara) and becomes Soviet land (infobox 'Part of USSR: 27 October 1924').

1924, 27 October: the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic is divided between the Uzbek SSR, the Turkmen SSR and the Karakalpak Autonomous Oblast and becomes Soviet land (page: 'On 27 October 1924 the Khorezm SSR was divided').
1925: Japan leaves northern Sakhalin.
1926, 15 April: the Soviet Union annexes Franz Josef Land.
1939, 17 September: the Red Army invades Poland.
1939, 28 September: Germany and the USSR fix the partition line.
1939: the Soviet Union annexes eastern Poland.
1939, 30 November: the Red Army invades Finland.
1940, March: the Winter War ends.
1940, March: Finland cedes Karelia to the Soviet Union.
1940, 28 June to 4 July: the Soviet Union takes Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina from Romania.
1940, 3 August: Lithuania is incorporated into the Soviet Union.
1940, 5 August: Latvia is incorporated into the Soviet Union.
1940, 6 August: Estonia is incorporated into the Soviet Union (see Lithuania and Latvia for the June ultimata).
1941, 22 June: Germany invades the Soviet Union.
1941, July: Germany occupies the Baltic states.
1941, July: Belarus and the Smolensk road fall.
1941, July: Romania retakes Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina.
1941, 25 August: British and Soviet forces invade Iran.
1941, August: Finland retakes the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia in the Continuation War.
1941, September: most of Ukraine is lost.
1942, 3 July: Sevastopol falls and Crimea is lost.
1942, 23 August: German troops reach the Volga at Stalingrad.
1943, 31 January: the Germans surrender at Stalingrad.
1943, 22 August: Kharkov is abandoned for the last time.
1943, November: the Red Army retakes Kyiv.
1944: the Red Army retakes most of the Baltic states.
1944: the Red Army clears Belarus, the rest of Ukraine, western Russia and Moldova.
1944, 22 June to 19 August: Operation Bagration clears Belarus.
1944, August: the Soviet Union retakes Bessarabia.
1944, 19 September: the Moscow Armistice returns the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia to the Soviet Union.
1944, 11 October: Tuva joins the Soviet Union.
1944, 15 October: the Red Army takes Petsamo, which Finland ceded in the armistice.
1944, 11 October: Tuva joins the Soviet Union.
1945, 8 May: the war in Europe ends.
1945, 10 May: the Courland Pocket capitulates.
1945, June: the Soviet zone of Germany.
1945, 29 June: Czechoslovakia cedes Carpathian Ruthenia.
1945, August: northern East Prussia goes under Soviet administration.
1945, 9 August: the Soviet Union invades Manchuria.
1945, August: the Red Army occupies Manchuria.
1945, August: the Red Army occupies Inner Mongolia.
1945, August: the Soviet Union takes South Sakhalin.
1945, 24 August: the Soviet Union takes the north of Korea.
1945, August: the Soviet Union returns the Bialystok area to Poland.
ledger.cpn: Poland (Polish People's Republic and Third Polish Republic)

ledger.x: 1945, 9 August: the Soviet invasion of Manchuria begins (infobox 'Soviet invasion: 9 August 1945' in the manchukuo dossier; this page: the Soviets 'commenced their invasion simultaneously on three fronts' on 9 August 1945).
Late August 1945: the fighting in Manchuria ends and Manchukuo is dissolved (manchukuo /ledger/10 and /ledger/15); the occupation events follow with the Republic of China as counterpart.
1945, 2 September: the Soviet-Japanese war ends.
1945, September: the Kuril Islands are taken.
1946: the Red Army leaves Manchuria.
1946: the Red Army leaves Inner Mongolia (see Manchuria).
1946, May: the Red Army leaves Iran.
1948, December: Soviet forces leave northern Korea.
1949, 7 October: the Soviet zone ends with the German Democratic Republic.
1979: the Soviet army enters Afghanistan.
1989: the Soviet army leaves Afghanistan.
1990, 11 March: Lithuania declares independence.
1990, 30 March: Estonia begins its transition to independence.
1990, 4 May: Latvia declares the restoration of independence.
1991, 6 September: the Soviet Union recognises Lithuania.
1991, 6 September: the Soviet Union recognises Estonia (Estonia had restored independence on the night of 20 August).
1991, 6 September: the Soviet Union recognises Latvia.
1991, 6 September: Lithuania leaves the Union.
1991, 6 September: Estonia leaves the Union.
1991, 6 September: Latvia leaves the Union.
1991, 26 December: the Soviet Union ceases to exist.

wars.name: Russian Civil War: the Far Eastern end
wars.outcome: The Japanese Army 'announced on 24 June 1922 that it would remove all of its troops from Siberia by the end of October'; the Far Eastern Republic's army retook Vladivostok on 25 October 1922 and Soviet Russia absorbed the Republic on 15 November 1922, before…

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: The Red Army invaded on 17 September 1939; the 28 September 1939 Boundary and Friendship Treaty fixed the partition and eastern Poland was converted into Soviet republics after staged elections.

wars.name: Winter War
wars.outcome: Invaded on 30 November 1939; in March 1940 Finland ceded parts of Karelia, Kuusamo and Salla and leased Hanko as a naval base.

wars.name: Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina
wars.outcome: After the ultimatum of 26 June 1940 and Romania's acceptance two days later, the Soviet Union 'occupied and annexed' Bessarabia between 28 June and 4 July; the Hertsa region was taken later by force.

wars.name: Soviet occupation of the Baltic states
wars.outcome: Ultimata of 15 and 16 June 1940, occupation by the Red Army, then incorporation on 3, 5 and 6 August 1940.

wars.name: Eastern Front (World War II)
wars.outcome: Barbarossa began on 22 June 1941; the Axis reached the Volga on 23 August 1942; Stalingrad fell on 31 January 1943; Kharkov (22 August 1943) and Kyiv (November 1943) were retaken; the front ended with the capture of Berlin and the German surrender of 8-9 May…

wars.name: Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran
wars.outcome: Invaded on 25 August 1941; Iran surrendered on 31 August; the Soviets held the north until May 1946, past the 2 March 1946 deadline of the Tripartite Treaty.

wars.name: Soviet-Japanese War
wars.outcome: The Soviet invasion began on 9 August 1945 and the campaign ended on 2 September 1945; South Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands were annexed, Manchuria and Inner Mongolia occupied until 1946 and Korea divided at the 38th parallel.

wars.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1956 (Soviet suppression)
wars.outcome: Listed on the Soviet Union page among the uprisings the Soviet military suppressed; no border moved.

wars.name: Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia
wars.outcome: 'The invasion of Czechoslovakia (1968)' is on the Soviet Union page's list of Soviet military actions; the page gives no month and no result, and Czechoslovakia stays a sovereign state.

wars.name: Soviet-Afghan War
wars.outcome: 'The Soviet Union also began the war in Afghanistan between 1979 and 1989.'

wars.name: Continuation War
wars.outcome: Finland retook the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia in August-September 1941; the Vyborg-Petrozavodsk offensive of June-August 1944 drove it out ('recaptured Viipuri ... on 20 June'); the Moscow Armistice of 19 September 1944 restored the 1940 border and…
